constraints.name: no_self_loop
constraints.description: No station is connected to itself; xi ≠ yi.

constraints.name: no_multiple_edges
constraints.description: Between each pair of stations there is at most one passage.

constraints.name: undirected_graph
constraints.description: Passages can be used to travel in both directions; the graph is undirected.

constraints.name: graph_connectivity
constraints.description: One can reach any station from any other station along the passages.

constraints.name: exactly_one_cycle
constraints.description: The subway scheme contains exactly one simple cycle (ringroad) that does not repeat any station.

objective.description: Compute the shortest distance from each node to the unique cycle in the graph

invariants.name: unique_cycle
invariants.description: The input graph contains exactly one simple cycle, and the rest of the graph forms trees attached to that cycle. This property is guaranteed by the problem statement and is relied upon by the algorithm to identify the single cycle and then compute distances outward from it.

properties.remaining_components: acyclic trees rooted at cycle vertices

invariants.name: dfs_visit_state_progression
invariants.description: In the first DFS, each vertex follows a strict state order: 0 (unvisited) → 1 (in recursion stack) → 2 (fully processed). No state ever transitions backward. A cycle is detected when the DFS encounters an edge to a neighbor that is already in state 1 and is not the immediate parent.

invariants.name: distance_increasing_property
invariants.description: During the second DFS (or BFS), distances are assigned so that all cycle vertices have distance 0, and for any tree-edge (u,v) where u is already visited, dist[v] = dist[u] + 1. This ensures each vertex's final distance equals its shortest-path distance to the cycle.

properties.propagation_rule: dist[v] = dist[u] + 1 for tree-edge (u,v) when u is visited first
properties.optimality: each vertex's distance equals the minimum number of edges to any cycle vertex
